name: Tauri
summary: A desktop application framework that hosts webviews in a native Rust application, routes frontend calls through command IPC, and constrains native capabilities with explicit permissions and capabilities.

features.name: Native shell and webview composition
features.description: Tauri represents windows and webviews as native runtime objects. A window may host one or more webviews, and the runtime abstraction delegates platform-specific window and webview operations to a selected implementation such as tao and wry.
benefits: Uses native application infrastructure while retaining web UI development
Allows multiple webviews to be composed within native windows
costs: Webview behavior varies with the operating system runtime
Window and webview lifecycles require coordination across Rust and frontend code

features.name: Command invoke IPC
features.description: Frontend code invokes registered Rust commands through Tauri's IPC protocol. Command dispatch deserializes arguments, identifies the calling webview, executes the handler, and serializes a result or error back to the frontend.
benefits: Creates an explicit typed boundary for native operations
Supports asynchronous request/response and streaming channel patterns
costs: Serialization and command registration add protocol surface
Commands must handle caller context and errors explicitly

features.name: Capability and permission authority
features.description: Tauri resolves capabilities and permissions to determine which windows or webviews may access commands and resources. The ACL implementation and schema generator make permissions, scopes, and platform-specific capability selection explicit configuration inputs.
benefits: Restricts native APIs by application context instead of exposing all commands globally
Makes privilege configuration reviewable and declarative
costs: Capability configuration becomes part of application correctness
Permission and scope changes can alter runtime behavior without changing command code

features.name: Asset and runtime packaging boundary
features.description: Tauri packages a Rust native executable with frontend assets and a platform webview runtime rather than bundling a complete browser engine. The CLI templates and runtime APIs expose application asset URLs, webview creation, and platform-specific packaging as separate boundaries.
benefits: Can reduce bundled runtime size by using the platform webview
Separates frontend assets from native command implementation
costs: Installed webview versions and platform policy affect compatibility
Asset protocols and packaging configuration require platform validation

mathematical_views.question: Which webviews and windows can reach which native commands under a capability configuration?
assumptions: Windows and webviews are context nodes
Commands and permissions are capability nodes
An allowed edge denotes configured authority, not successful business behavior

mathematical_views.question: How does a frontend invoke transition through protocol decoding, command execution, and response serialization?
assumptions: Each invoke has a command identifier and serialized arguments
The calling webview is part of dispatch state
Transport scheduling and webview implementation details are abstracted

mathematical_views.question: Which web UI operations are refined into native window, resource, or command operations?
assumptions: Frontend requests are mapped to native runtime operations
Platform webview capabilities are not assumed identical
The relation is explanatory and does not prove cross-platform equivalence

benefits: Native window integration with web-based UI

costs: Registration, serialization, and errors must be maintained

benefits: Declarative least-authority control over native APIs
costs: ACL configuration adds a second source of runtime behavior

benefits: Smaller native distribution than bundling a full browser engine
costs: Platform-installed webview behavior becomes a deployment dependency
